definition: Social neuroscience is an interdisciplinary area that examines how social experiences and relationships are connected with psychological processes and the brain systems that support them. In this packet, it is described as integrating psychology with developmental and social neuroscience to understand socially embedded behavior and learning through reciprocal links between social context, motivation and emotion, and neural processes.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “social neuroscience” as a discipline in general terms; it describes an “integrative neuroeducational model” and an interdisciplinary approach combining educational science, psychology, and developmental/social neuroscience, rather than stating a general definition of the field.

The definition’s wording (“how social experiences and relationships are connected with psychological processes and the brain systems that support them”) is broader than what the packet explicitly asserts; the packet focuses on adolescents’ socio-emotional experiences at school and related neural mechanisms rather than providing a general characterization of social neuroscience.
